claim: Adgrg6 (Gpr126) is an adhesion class G protein-coupled receptor with a conserved role in myelination of the peripheral nervous system.
source: Adgrg6 (Gpr126) is an adhesion class G protein-coupled receptor with a conserved role in myelination of the peripheral nervous system.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing this role.

claim: In the zebrafish, mutation of adgrg6 results in defects in the inner ear where otic tissue fails to down-regulate versican gene expression and morphogenesis is disrupted.
source: In the zebrafish, mutation of adgrg6 also results in defects in the inner ear: otic tissue fails to down-regulate versican gene expression and morphogenesis is disrupted.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior published work and data presented in the manuscript.

claim: From a screen of 3120 structurally diverse compounds, 68 compounds were identified that reduce versican b expression in the adgrg6 mutant ear.
source: From a screen of 3120 structurally diverse compounds, we have identified 68 that reduce versican b expression in the adgrg6 mutant ear
evidence: This claim is directly supported by the experimental data from the primary screen described in the manuscript.

claim: 41 compounds that reduce versican b expression also restore myelin basic protein gene expression in Schwann cells of mutant embryos.
source: 41 of which also restore myelin basic protein gene expression in Schwann cells of mutant embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by the secondary screen data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nineteen compounds unable to rescue a strong adgrg6 allele provide candidates for molecules that may interact directly with the Adgrg6 receptor.
source: Nineteen compounds unable to rescue a strong adgrg6 allele provide candidates for molecules that may interact directly with the Adgrg6 receptor.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differential rescue of weak versus strong alleles.

claim: In homozygous loss-of-function adgrg6 zebrafish and mouse mutants, peripheral myelination is severely impaired.
source: In homozygous loss-of-function adgrg6 zebrafish and mouse mutants, peripheral myelination is severely impaired: Schwann cells associate with axons, but are unable to generate the myelin sheath, and show reduced expression of the myelin basic protein (mbp) gene (Glenn and Talbot, 2013; Mogha et al., 2013; Monk et al., 2009; Monk et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Schwann cells in adgrg6 mutants associate with axons but are unable to generate the myelin sheath.
source: Schwann cells associate with axons, but are unable to generate the myelin sheath, and show reduced expression of the myelin basic protein (mbp) gene (Glenn and Talbot, 2013; Mogha et al., 2013; Monk et al., 2009; Monk et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Schwann cells in adgrg6 mutants show reduced expression of the myelin basic protein (mbp) gene.
source: Schwann cells associate with axons, but are unable to generate the myelin sheath, and show reduced expression of the myelin basic protein (mbp) gene (Glenn and Talbot, 2013; Mogha et al., 2013; Monk et al., 2009; Monk et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Targeted disruption of Adgrg6 in the mouse results in limb and cardiac abnormalities, axon degeneration and embryonic lethality.
source: Targeted disruption of Adgrg6 in the mouse results in additional abnormal phenotypes, including limb and cardiac abnormalities, axon degeneration and embryonic lethality (Monk et al., 2011; Patra et al., 2013; Waller-Evans et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In humans, mutations in ADGRG6 are causative for congenital contracture syndrome 9, a severe type of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita.
source: In humans, mutations in ADGRG6 are causative for congenital contracture syndrome 9, a severe type of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (Ravenscroft et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Peripheral nerves from individuals with ADGRG6 mutations have reduced expression of myelin basic protein.
source: Peripheral nerves from affected individuals have reduced expression of myelin basic protein, suggesting that the function of ADGRG6 in myelination is evolutionarily conserved from teleosts to humans (Ravenscroft et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The function of ADGRG6 in myelination is evolutionarily conserved from teleosts to humans.
source: Peripheral nerves from affected individuals have reduced expression of myelin basic protein, suggesting that the function of ADGRG6 in myelination is evolutionarily conserved from teleosts to humans (Ravenscroft et al., 2015).
